title: Post-2020 climate agreements in the major economies assessed in the light of global models
field: Integrated assessment modeling of climate policy
problem: The paper addresses the challenge of coordinating post-2020 climate policies by providing quantitative, regional-level information on emission pathways, carbon budgets, and distributional costs for major economies, which has been limited in previous global-focused model intercomparison studies, thereby hindering effective and equitable international policy negotiation.
method: This paper reviews scenario results from a model intercomparison project, using multiple integrated assessment models to quantify the implications of different post-2020 climate agreements for major economies by assessing regional emission pathways, carbon budgets, mitigation costs, and distributional consequences.
task: The task is to use integrated assessment models to quantify and assess the implications of different post-2020 international climate agreements for major economies, focusing on emission peaking, carbon budgets, mitigation costs, and the distributional consequences of various policy scenarios.
innovation: This paper synthesizes scenario results from a model intercomparison project to quantify the implications of post-2020 climate agreements for major economies, assessing regional emission peaking years, carbon budgets, and the distributional consequences of different policy pathways to inform international negotiations.
